title: Takeda Turns to SAP S/4HANA to Support Digital Transformation
summary: Takeda Pharmaceuticals uses RISE with SAP to migrate to SAP Cloud ERP, helping to streamline operations, embed AI, and enhance patient care.
body_markdown:
Takeda Pharmaceuticals is in the midst of a major shift in how it runs some of its most important business processes. The biotech company’s move from SAP ERP Central Component (SAP ECC) to[SAP Cloud ERP](https://www.sap.com/products/erp.html) applications through the[RISE with SAP](https://www.sap.com/products/erp/rise.html) journey is part of a broader effort to simplify how its business runs, make better use of data, and create more room for digital and AI-enabled ways of working.


Takeda has 250 years of history, 50,000 employees, global operations, and medicines reaching patients in more than 80 countries. That’s why it’s important for the transformation project to connect everyday process improvements with a larger purpose: helping employees work more effectively and supporting the reliable delivery of medicines to patients.


“A couple of years ago, around 2022 or 2023, Takeda decided to make data and digital capabilities a core part of our business strategy,” said Roland Straub, global business transformation lead for Supply Chain at Takeda Pharmaceuticals. “With the AI developments of the last few years, we see a real opportunity to bring automation and support to life for our employees and, importantly, for our patients.”


### [Takeda Brings Data and Digital to Life with SAP](https://youtu.be/j5CtFYaJiNs)

[SAP Cloud ERP](https://news.sap.com/tags/cloud-erp/) offers an integrated suite of business applications that can support core business processes. For organizations moving from SAP ECC, the shift can also be an opportunity to simplify processes, reduce complexity, and prepare the business for more embedded intelligence.


Straub explained why that foundation matters to Takeda: “SAP is the core system that supports and operates nearly all of our processes around the globe, from manufacturing and supply chain to finance, quality, and beyond.”


The transformation reflects SAP’s work to embed AI capabilities throughout business processes. The Autonomous Enterprise is SAP’s vision for how businesses can operate with people in control, systems working in context, and governance built in.


That balance is especially important in regulated industries such as life sciences. Autonomous regulated manufacturing scenarios can help connect supply chain, production, and quality processes while supporting consistency, reducing manual effort, and maintaining compliance boundaries.


Takeda is also working with SAP on co-development in this area. “Together, we are co-developing new agentic functionalities for regulated industries,” Straub said. “We believe these capabilities can scale across the industry, not just within Takeda.”


Looking ahead, Straub said the priorities are clear: bring the SAP S/4HANA journey to life, understand and use the AI capabilities in SAP Cloud ERP effectively, and continue building the partnership with SAP. For Takeda, success goes beyond just a technology go-live. It’s a more connected, intelligent, and patient-focused way of working.
